next_action.description: Fix the detection colour. Root cause is structural, not cosmetic: MaskManager._recomposite() UNIONS the manual layer and the selected autoPickMasks into ONE maskCanvas, and MpiCanvas._renderOverlay() draws that single canvas - so a detected region and a painted region are indistinguishable by construction. Split the DISPLAY, never the EXPORT: render the manual layer in the current white and the auto-pick layer in green as a second overlay pass (both still minus subtractCanvas), while getURL() / getMaskDataURL() keep emitting the SINGLE unioned black-and-white mask every consumer downstream expects. Watch three things in _renderOverlay: the displayInverted branch recolours through a scratch buffer with source-atop, maskOpacity is applied as globalAlpha around the whole draw, and the dots are drawn on top afterwards. Then ask the user which UI polish they want before touching layout.

key_decisions: PHASE A FIRST, PHASE B AFTER. Phase A = Impact Pack Mask Pointer on the sam_vit_b_01ec64.pth weight the auto-mask graph ALREADY loads. Zero download, zero licence, zero dependency entry.

The points branch converts its MASK back to SEGS with MaskToSEGS(combined=True) and rejoins the EXISTING ImpactSEGSPicker -> ImpactSEGSToMaskList chain. That is what let the thumbs / pick / composite plumbing be reused rather than forked, and it keeps the shipped 1.2.0 one-mask-per-pick contract intact.

Points mode auto-picks index 0 up front, so a points run is ONE round trip. The detector's detect-then-pick two-step exists because YOLO returns N segments to choose between; the mask-points branch returns exactly one region, so there is nothing to choose.

The two detector branches sit behind a second MpiIfElse titled Input_Points_Mode. Its inputs are lazy (check_lazy_status), so only the selected branch executes - points mode never runs YOLO and vice versa.

Dot polarity is carried by RADIUS, not by a separate mask: MaskManager synthesizes r=8 for positive and r=4 for negative, straddling the exact 10px bbox-width cliff that mask_hint_use_negative='Small' uses. PROVEN live at 6.10x separation. The graph node now has mask_hint_use_negative='Small'.

The dots mask is rendered at SOURCE image resolution, NOT the MASK_MAX_EDGE-capped working size. Two reasons: SEG coords must line up with the image SAMDetectorCombined receives, and the negative cliff is measured in that image's own pixels.
The dots ship as white on BLACK through ImageToMask(channel=red), deliberately not as an alpha mask - LoadImage-family MASK outputs are 1-alpha and that inversion is a known foot-gun.

Add / Subtract is APP-SIDE via MaskManager.bakeAutoPicksInto(), which writes BOTH layers the way paint() does: adding un-erases, subtracting un-paints. No AddMask/SubtractMask nodes, no extra round trip, undo preserved, composes with the brush.
The Scope slider ships the raw threshold 30-99 with no remapping and no MpiNormalizeValue rig - the user proposed then retracted that. An info box carries the sweep-do-not-nudge advice instead.
The old YOLO detector path is KEPT as the fast one-click Face / Hair / Hand / Person shortcut. Points sit BESIDE it.
Add / Subtract buttons are shown in points mode only, so the detector's existing UX is untouched.
constraints: THE CONVERTER HAS BLAST RADIUS. Running `node scripts/workflow-to-api.mjs` with NO ARGUMENTS re-emits ALL 31 workflows and additionally writes 15 stray comfy_workflows/*_template.json files that do not belong there. Convert ONE file instead: `node scripts/workflow-to-api.mjs comfy_workflows/raw/img_auto_mask.json` prints to stdout, then write it with JSON.stringify(wf, null, 2) + a trailing newline - that byte format matches what the batch writer produces, verified by diff.
getURL() / getMaskDataURL() MUST keep emitting one unioned black-and-white mask. Every mask consumer downstream reads it. The colour fix is a DISPLAY-only split.

MpiCanvasViewer already has its own contextmenu handler on its root that pops the image context menu. InputController's points-mode handler therefore calls stopPropagation as well as preventDefault - that line is load-bearing, do not simplify it away.
MpiAutoMaskThumbs.setPicks() deliberately does NOT emit 'change'. Points mode relies on that to restore pick 0 after setImages() clears the selection without re-triggering the run.

N DOTS DO NOT GIVE N OBJECTS. Every point goes into ONE sam_obj.predict call, so SAM returns a SINGLE region consistent with ALL points. This was re-confirmed by accident in the polarity test: two positive dots gave the whole person. One part per run is the shape of the feature; Add accumulates parts across runs.

threshold is NOT a smooth confidence. sam_predict keeps every SAM candidate scoring >= threshold and unions them, falling back to the single best if none pass. SAM emits 3 candidates, so the dial SNAPS between 3 states and 0.50 -> 0.60 is usually identical. Sweep it, do not nudge it.
dilation STAYS AT 0. The user verified on the bench that it grows into unwanted areas because it blindly dilates whatever SAM returned, scatter included.
The scatter cleanup pair (GrowMaskWithBlur -4 then +4 with fill_holes) MUST stay equal and opposite or the mask grows or shrinks overall. 4/4 is the shipping default.
MpiLoadImageFromPath still EXECUTES in detector mode (it emits a preview) but self-gates on the empty path via ExecutionBlocker, so nothing downstream of it runs. That is expected, not a leak.

A data: URL in a media param is staged to a real file by comfyController (and uploaded to the Pod on a remote engine) automatically, because the param's same-titled node is in PATH_MEDIA_CLASSES. Input_Points_Mask needed no new plumbing for either engine.
MPI-246 trap checked and NOT applicable - none of the eight added nodes self-builds a path enum, so no SLASH_ONLY_NODE_TYPES entry is needed.
The remote engine path has NOT been exercised for points mode. It should work by construction (same upload path as Input_Image) but nobody has run it on a Pod.
Do not run git against sibling folders from this repo, and commit by explicit pathspec only - never git add -A.
